catalog_quote: Unfortunately, the informant dictated his stories in a manner too slow and too loose for me to get an impression of the patterns of intonation and stress. I. TONES This dialect is a tonal language. Tones are the contrasting contours of pitch. There are eight tones, but there are only seven phonemic tones inasmuch as the first two tones are in complentary distribution. [...] (1) 34, a lower rising tone, occurs only in the syllables with aspirated initials and [s-] and [ɸ-]; 44, the second high level tone, occurs in the syllables with all other initials. These two tones are two alternants of one phoneme.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Yi Miao of Ke-Cheng Chai (Guangshun) is a tone language with eight surface tones / seven tonemes: 1 = 34 (after aspirated initials, s-, ɸ-) ~ 44 (elsewhere), 2 = 55, 3 = 45, 4 = 31, 5 = 33, 6 = 22, 7 = 21 (Chao digits); tones 2, 4, 6, 7 never occur after aspirated initials, s-, ɸ- or ʔ-. The author explicitly states he could NOT form an impression of stress or intonation patterns, so no word-stress claim is made.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone 1's two values 34/44 are conditioned by initial aspiration; tones 2, 4, 6, 7 restricted to unaspirated initials; final -eŋ mainly in Chinese loans. No tone sandhi described in this article.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.3 makes this the Glottolog's most extensive description of sout2756 and its languoid note equates 'Yi Miao.. from Ke-Cheng Chai 格正寨 in Kwang-Shun 廣順 district = Changshun Yi Miao = Southwestern Guiyang Hmong [hmg]'. Independent support: Wang 1985: 104 lists 长顺县广顺 among the places of the Guiyang subdialect's 西南土语; the system Chang describes (tone 1 realised 34 after aspirates/s/ɸ vs 44 elsewhere, tones 2/4/6/7 excluded after aspirates; prenasalised stops, aspirated nasals, pl/pr/ql-type clusters, uvulars) shows the aspiration-conditioned tone split characteristic of the Guiyang subdialect.) and Huishui (hmc/hmh) varieties further south; Chang calls the group 'Yi Miao' (his informant a 'Hei Miao'), an exonym not used in the PRC classification. Our earlier scan had this title as 'Chang 1957 on a related variety' without opening it.

new_statements.quote: 清镇8个支系苗族语言均属于川黔滇方言，以“青苗”为例，属于川黔滇方言贵阳次方言西南土语。 苗语声母多，韵母少。各方言都有塞擦音，绝大多数地区有小舌塞音、清鼻音、清边音等，除黔东方言外，都有鼻冠塞音、鼻冠塞擦音。现代苗语各方言有3～13个声调不等，而普遍都有6～8个不同的声调。以“青苗”的塘边寨苗语为例，塘边寨苗语有声母50个，韵母15个，声调7个。
new_statements.translation: The languages of all eight Miao subgroups of Qingzhen belong to the Chuanqiandian dialect; taking the 'Qing Miao' as the example, [their speech] belongs to the Southwestern vernacular of the Guiyang subdialect of the Chuanqiandian dialect. Miao has many initials and few finals. All dialects have affricates, most areas have uvular stops, voiceless nasals, voiceless laterals etc., and all except the Qiandong dialect have prenasalised stops and affricates. Modern Miao dialects have from 3 to 13 tones, generally 6 to 8 distinct tones. Taking the Tangbianzhai speech of the 'Qing Miao' as the example, Tangbianzhai Miao has 50 initials, 15 finals and 7 tones.

The entry has no 重音/轻声/变调/连读 anywhere; it is a tone-inventory count (50 initials, 15 finals, 7 tones for Tangbianzhai Qing Miao) inside a local encyclopedia, so reading tone language, no stress statement / statement_type tone are right and 'other' is the right contents class. Identity: the entry itself assigns Qingzhen Qing Miao to 川黔滇方言贵阳次方言西南土语 (= hmg) and Tangbianzhai (红枫湖镇) faces Pingba Machang/Baiyun, the hmg core of Wang 1985:104, across the Hongfeng reservoir; I keep 'probably' rather than 'yes' o…
new_statements.relation_note: 7 tones, 50 initials, 15 finals for Tangbianzhai Qing Miao; general Miao remarks (uvulars, voiceless nasals/laterals, prenasalised stops); 2005 language-vitality figures per Qingzhen subgroup (四印苗 100% speakers, 青苗 52.44%, 须须苗 31.8%, 素苗 19.2%, 花苗 nearly extinct)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tangbianzhai (Qingzhen Qing Miao, Guiyang subdialect SW vernacular) is tonal with 7 tones (50 initials, 15 finals); nothing is said about stress, weak syllables or sandhi.
new_statements.exceptions: none; no tone values, no sandhi, no 轻声/重音 remark
new_statements.identity_note: The entry itself assigns the variety: '清镇8个支系苗族语言均属于川黔滇方言，以“青苗”为例，属于川黔滇方言贵阳次方言西南土语' and the figures are for the Qing Miao of 塘边寨 (红枫湖镇塘边村, Qingzhen; the same encyclopedia's 塘边寨 entry calls it a '青苗聚居地'). Wang 1985:104 and 中国语言文字学大辞典 2007 list Qingzhen localities in the SW vernacular [hmg] area, so the assignment is consistent; Qingzhen's 四印苗/白苗 speak other (Chuanqiandian-subdialect) vernaculars, but the numbers quoted are explicitly for the Qing Miao point. Secondhand local-encyclopedia summary, almost certainly drawn from 清镇县民族志 (1992, work 2) or 清镇市苗学会 materials.

sources.note: Abstracts only. Xiao's thesis abstract explicitly assigns Pingba Huagaolin Miao to the Chuanqiandian subdialect, not Guiyang (so not hmg); Yang 2010 = sound correspondences; Tang 2019 = tone register/phonation of Anshun Dadongkou Miao (subdialect unstated). No abstract mentions 重音/轻声 for a Guiyang variety. Queries 清镇苗语 and 凯洒 returned nothing relevant.
